newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says it has world's lowest murder rate.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says it has world's lowest murder rate.

text.p: Cuba said on Monday it had the world's lowest murder rate.

National police chief and deputy Interior Minister Gen. Romarico Sotomayor told the weekly newspaper Trabajadores the Communist-ruled island had the lowest homicide rate in the world. But he gave no figures.

Crime is rarely reported in Cuba's state-run news media so it is hard to get an idea of how many murders are committed each year among the country's 11 million inhabitants. The media usually present violent crime as one of the scourges of capitalist societies such as the United States.

Sotomayor said crime rates rose in Cuba during the economic crisis unleashed in 1990 by the collapse of the Soviet Union, Cuba's main trade and aid partner. But he said it never reached levels experienced by many other nations.

House burglaries and thefts of cars in cities such as Havana do appear to be a fairly frequent. And for foreign tourists, handbag-snatching, although rarely with violence, is also a threat in some parts of Havana.
